source_text: Febrem denique inter ceteros mortiferos et cruciarios exitus erogando homini deputatam neque quia est miramur, est enim, neque quia erogat hominem, ad hoc enim est. Proinde haereses ad languorem et interitum fidei productas si expavescimus hoc posse, prius est ut expavescamus hoc eas esse, quae dum sunt, habent posse, et dum possunt, habent esse. Sed enim febrem ut malum et de causa et de potentia sua, ut notum est, abominamur potius quam miramur et, quantum in nobis est, praecavemus, non habentes abolitionem eius in nostra potestate. Haereses vero mortem aeternam et maioris ignis ardorem inferentes malunt quidam mirari quod hoc possint quam devitare ne possint, cum habeant devitandi potestatem. Ceterum nihil valebunt, si illas tantum valere non mirentur. Aut enim dum mirantur, in scandalum subministrantur, aut quia scandalizantur, ideo mirantur quasi quod tantum valeant ex aliqua veniat veritate. Mirum scilicet, ut malum vires suas habeat; nisi quod haereses apud eos multum valeant qui in fide non valent. In pugna pugilum et gladiatorum plerumque non quia fortis est vincit quis, aut quia non potest vinci, sed quoniam ille qui victus est nullis viribus fuit: adeo idem ille victor, bene valenti postea comparatus, etiam superatus recedit. Non aliter haereses de quorundam infirmitatibus habent quod valent, nihil valentes, si in bene valentem fidem incurrant.
thought_title: Heresies have power only over the weak in faith
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heresies, like fever, should not be wondered at for their power, because their power comes only from the weakness of those they overcome.
pass_a_gloss: Fever, finally, among the other deadly and torturous ends, has been allotted to man for destroying him, and we do not wonder either because it exists, for it does exist, or because it destroys man, for it exists for this purpose. Likewise, if we are terrified that heresies, produced for the weakening and destruction of faith, have this power, first we must be terrified that they exist, since while they exist, they have power, and while they have power, they exist. But indeed fever, as an evil both from its cause and from its power, as is known, we abhor rather than wonder at, and, as far as is in us, we take precautions against it, not having the abolition of it in our power. But heresies, bringing in eternal death and the burning of a greater fire, some people prefer to wonder that they have this power rather than to avoid it so that they may not have it, although they have the power of avoiding it. Otherwise, they will have no strength, if people do not wonder that they have so much strength. For either while they wonder, they are supplied for scandal, or because they are scandalized, for this reason they wonder, as if the fact that they have so much strength comes from some truth. Wonderful, of course, that evil should have its own strength; except that heresies have much strength among those who have no strength in faith. In the fight of boxers and gladiators, usually someone wins not because he is strong, or because he cannot be defeated, but because the one who was defeated had no strength: so much so that the same victor, compared afterwards with one in good health, even departs defeated. Not otherwise do heresies have what strength they have from the weaknesses of certain people, having no strength, if they run against a faith in good health.

choices.why: erogare here means to consume or destroy, as a fever consumes a person; the gerundive expresses purpose

choices.term: ad languorem et interitum fidei productas
choices.english: produced for the weakening and destruction of faith
choices.why: languor means weakness or feebleness, and interitus means destruction; productas means brought forth or produced
rejected: brought forth for the sickness and ruin of faith
produced for the languor and death of faith

choices.english: the burning of a greater fire
choices.why: ardor is the burning heat, and maioris ignis is a greater fire, referring to a more severe punishment
rejected: the heat of a greater fire
the flame of a greater fire

choices.why: subministrantur means they are supplied or furnished; scandalum is scandal or stumbling block
bene valere means to be in good health, used here metaphorically for strong faith

choices.english: run against a faith in good health
choices.why: incurro means to run into or against; the metaphor is of heresies attacking a healthy faith
rejected: encounter a faith in good health

pass_b_english: Consider fever, which among the other deadly and torturous ends has been allotted to man for his destruction. We are not astonished that it exists—it does exist—nor that it destroys man, for that is why it exists. In the same way, if we are terrified that heresies, produced for the weakening and destruction of faith, have this power, we should first be terrified that they exist at all. For while they exist, they have power, and while they have power, they exist.

But fever, as an evil, we abhor rather than marvel at, both because of its cause and its power, as is well known; and as far as lies in us, we take precautions against it, since we do not have its abolition in our own power. Heresies, however, bring eternal death and the burning of a greater fire, yet some people prefer to marvel that they have this power rather than to avoid it, even though they have the power to avoid them. But they will have no strength at all if people do not marvel at their strength.

For either while people marvel, heresies are supplied for scandal, or because people are scandalized, they marvel—as if such great power could come from some truth. A fine marvel indeed, that evil should have its own strength! Except that heresies have much power among those who have no power in faith. In a contest of boxers and gladiators, a man does not usually win because he is strong, or because he cannot be beaten, but because the one who was defeated had no strength at all. So that same victor, when later matched against someone in good health, goes away defeated. In just the same way, heresies draw their strength from the weaknesses of certain people, and have no strength at all if they run against a faith in good health.
